diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any fixed $\psi \in H^{\kappa+2}(\Omega)$ with $\kappa$ as in (\ref{ks}), let $$\bar \psi=\bar \psi_{\theta_0} = \mathcal I^{-1} \Delta \psi,$$ which by (\ref{fishinvbd}) and the Sobolev imbedding theorem defines an element of $$\bar \psi_{\theta_0} \in H^{\kappa}_0(\Omega) \subset C^2(\Omega) \subset L^2(\Omega).$$

issues.failure_explanation: Condition F provides \mathcal I^{-1} only as a bounded operator on H^\eta_0 for \eta \ge \eta_0, but the proof of Theorem mainbvm uses it at other levels. (i) Theorem laplaceapp and Lemma oldtimer require \bar\psi = \mathcal I^{-1}\Delta\psi with \|\bar\psi\|_{H^\kappa} \lesssim \|\psi\|_{H^{\kappa+2}} uniformly over \psi \in U(\kappa+2,B) (e.g. the bound '\bar \psi and then also p_N(\bar \psi) are uniformly bounded in H^{\kappa}' used in oldtimer's proof and in (fullbd)); this needs Condition F at level \eta=\kappa, i.e. \kappa \ge \eta_0. Yet (ks) only imposes \kappa > 2d+\zeta, and the hypothesis k > \max(\zeta+5d/2,\eta_0) does not guarantee \kappa \ge \eta_0 is feasible: if \eta_0 > 2d+\zeta and k \le \eta_0+d/2 then necessarily \kappa < \eta_0, and for generic \psi \in H^{\kappa+2} the object \bar\psi is not even defined. (ii) In (momhat) the displayed step \sum_j\lambda_j^{-k-2}\|\bar e_j\|^2 = \sum_j\lambda_j^{-k}\|\mathcal I^{-1}e_j\|_{L^2}^2 \le \sum_j\lambda_j^{-k}\|\mathcal I^{-2}e_j\|_{H^{\eta_0}}\|e_j\|_{H^{-\eta_0}} implicitly requires \mathcal I^{-1} bounded on L^2_0 (or H^{-\eta_0}), which Condition F does not give; using only \|\mathcal I^{-1}e_j\|_{H^{\eta_0}} \lesssim \|e_j\|_{H^{\eta_0}} the series becomes \sum_j\lambda_j^{-k+\eta_0}, finite only for k > \eta_0+d/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add k > \eta_0+d/2 to the hypotheses of Theorem mainbvm, choose \kappa \ge \eta_0 in (ks), and estimate (momhat) directly via (fishinvbd) at level \eta_0, giving \sum_j \lambda_j^{-k+\eta_0} < \infty.
issues.overall_effect: In the part of mainbvm's stated regime with \eta_0 > 2d+\zeta and k \le \eta_0+d/2, the perturbation centring \bar\psi (hence laplaceapp and oldtimer) and the tightness/moment bound (momhat) (also used in (uiui) of prop:added-1) are not justified, leaving a gap in mainbvm's proof. In the reaction-diffusion application the constraints can still be met, since Theorem raf allows any \eta_0 > 2+d/2 and one can arrange \kappa \ge \eta_0 and k > \eta_0+d/2 within k > 3d.
issues.title: Inversion of the information operator used outside Condition F's regularity range
issues.why_classification: The repair adds a standard parameter constraint and substitutes a routine direct estimate using bounds already in the paper; the method, the form of all conclusions, and the application Theorems bvminv and ganzwien are preserved without any change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: J_N \in \mathbb N, J_N \simeq N \delta_N^2,~~K_N = K_{N,\bar \kappa} = \sqrt N \delta_N \max(1,J_N^{\gamma-\bar \kappa})

issues.failure_explanation: With \delta_N = N^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)} and J_N \simeq N\delta_N^2 = N^{d/(2\gamma+d)}, direct computation gives \delta_N^2\sqrt N J_N^{\gamma-\bar\kappa} = N^{((d-1)\gamma + d/2 - d\bar\kappa)/(2\gamma+d)}, which equals the claimed N^{-(\bar\kappa-d/2)/(2\gamma+d)} only when d=1. For d \in \{2,3\} the true exponent is negative iff \bar\kappa > ((d-1)/d)\gamma + 1/2, but the proof's own constraints force \bar\kappa < \kappa - d/2 < k - d, while the theorem only assumes k > \max(\zeta+5d/2,\eta_0). Hence for admissible parameters with k \le ((d-1)/d)\gamma + d + 1/2 (e.g. d=3, \gamma=12, 9 < k \le 11.5; or d=2, \gamma=9, 6 < k \le 7) no admissible choice of \bar\kappa makes the first-order Cameron-Martin term vanish; it diverges. Likewise the convergence in (quadbd) requires \kappa > ((d-1)/d)\gamma, which fails for small admissible \kappa when d \ge 2. Therefore the Cameron-Martin density is not o(1)-close to 1 on \bar\Theta_N, the identity (postbus0)-(postbus000) is not established, the ratio of integrals in Theorem laplaceapp is uncontrolled, and the bound (fullbd) used in Proposition prop:added-1 fails.

failure_location.quote: $$\frac{|t|}{\sqrt N} |\langle \theta, p_N(\bar \psi_{\theta_0})\rangle_{\mathcal H_N}| \lesssim |t| \delta_N K_{N, \bar \kappa} \lesssim \delta_N^2 \sqrt N J_N^{\gamma-\bar \kappa} = N^{-(\bar \kappa -d/2)/(2\gamma+d)} \to 0$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis on k in Theorem mainbvm to k > ((d-1)/d)\gamma + d + 1/2, choosing \bar\kappa > ((d-1)/d)\gamma + 1/2 and \kappa > \bar\kappa + d/2, and correspondingly restrict the range of k in Theorem bvminv; the corrected exponent then yields \delta_N K_N \to 0 and (quadbd), restoring (postbus0)-(postbus000).
issues.overall_effect: For d \ge 2 and the smaller admissible values of k, Theorem mainbvm's Wasserstein Bernstein-von Mises theorem is unproven as stated, and Theorem bvminv's claim that the conclusion holds for any k > 3d is only established for k > ((d-1)/d)\gamma + d + 1/2. Theorem ganzwien is unaffected because parabolic smoothing (Lemma bootcamp) allows any sufficiently large k, for which the proof does close.
issues.title: Cameron-Martin density rate identity is false for d >= 2; localisation ratio not shown to be 1+o(1) in part of the stated regime
issues.why_classification: No new proof architecture is needed and the headline result (Theorem ganzwien, the uniform-norm BvM) survives verbatim, but the stated scope of mainbvm/bvminv - the range of k, i.e. the negative-Sobolev topology in which the BvM is proved - is genuinely narrowed for d \ge 2, which is more than a local or typographical fix while leaving a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
straightforward calculations show that the first term in the preceding maximum is of order
$$\sqrt N \int_0^{\sigma_N} u^{-d/2\beta}du \lesssim \sqrt N \tilde \delta_N^{2- d/\beta}(\zeta)$$ while the second is of order
$$\sqrt {\log N} \tilde \delta^{1-2d/\beta}_N(\zeta).$$

issues.failure_explanation: Since g_{\theta,\psi} is the linearisation remainder, Condition C gives the quadratic bound Ef_{\theta,\psi}^2(Z) = T^{-1}\|g_{\theta,\psi}\|_{L^2(\mathcal X)}^2 \lesssim \|\theta_{(t,\psi)}-\theta_0\|_{L^2}^4 \lesssim \tilde\delta_N(\zeta)^4, i.e. \sigma_N \simeq \tilde\delta_N(\zeta)^2, and the printed chaining orders correspond exactly to this proxy: the first chaining term equals \sqrt N\,\tilde\delta_N(\zeta)\mathscr J_N(\sigma_N/\tilde\delta_N(\zeta)) \simeq \sqrt N\,\sigma_N^{1-d/2\beta}, which with \sigma_N \simeq \tilde\delta_N(\zeta)^2 is the printed \sqrt N\tilde\delta_N(\zeta)^{2-d/\beta}. But the proof instead defines \sigma_N^2 via Condition B (a linear bound), giving \sigma_N \simeq \tilde\delta_N(\zeta); with that proxy the first term is \sqrt N\,\tilde\delta_N(\zeta)^{1-d/2\beta}, whose N-exponent is 1/2 - \frac{\gamma}{2\gamma+d}\frac{\bar\gamma-\zeta}{\bar\gamma+1}(1-\frac{d}{2\beta}) > 0 for every admissible parameter choice (since \frac{\gamma}{2\gamma+d} < 1/2), so it diverges and the claimed o(1) does not follow as written.

failure_location.quote:
By Condition \ref{gemol}B and $L^2 \to L^2([0,T], L^2)$-continuity of $\mathbb I_{\theta_0}$, we can bound the `weak variances' uniformly in $\psi, \theta$ as
$$Ef_{\theta, \psi}^2(Z) \le C \big\| \theta - \theta_0 - \frac{t}{\sqrt N} p_N(\bar \psi_{\theta_0}) \big\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2 \lesssim \tilde \delta^2_N(\zeta) + \frac{1}{N}  \equiv \sigma_N^2,$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the weak variance by Condition C instead of Condition B: on \bar\Theta_N, Ef^2 \lesssim \|\theta_{(t,\psi)}-\theta_0\|_{L^2}^4 \lesssim \tilde\delta_N(\zeta)^4, so \sigma_N \simeq \tilde\delta_N(\zeta)^2; every subsequently printed order then becomes correct (first term \sqrt N\tilde\delta_N^{2-d/\beta} = o(1) under \beta > 2d and \gamma > 3\zeta+3d/2+2, the second term gaining an extra 1/\sqrt N slack).
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of Lemma oldtimer does not establish the two uniform o(1) empirical-process bounds; these feed the remainder control in Theorem laplaceapp and hence the whole proof of Theorem mainbvm and its consequences.
issues.title: Wrong variance proxy in Lemma oldtimer: with the stated \sigma_N the chaining bound diverges
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-step substitution of a hypothesis already assumed and verified in the paper (Condition C), after which all displayed chaining computations are correct as printed; no new lemma, estimate, or change of any conclusion is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\partial}{\partial t} r - \Delta r - f'(u_{\theta_0}) r = m,~~\text{where } m = f(u_{\theta_0+h}) - f(u_{\theta_0}) - f'(u_{\theta_0})(u_{\theta_0+h}-u_{\theta_0}),

issues.failure_explanation: By Taylor's formula m(t) = (1/2)f''(\tilde u(t)) w(t)^2 with w = u_{\theta_0+h}-u_{\theta_0}, so \|m(t)\|_{L^2} \le (1/2)\|f''\|_\infty \|w(t)\|_{L^4}^2, and the inequality \|w(t)\|_{L^4}^2 \lesssim \|w(t)\|_{L^2}^2 used in the display is false (on a probability space the reverse holds). It fails even within the theorem's hypotheses: take \theta_0=0 and f(x)=x^2 near 0 (so u_{\theta_0} \equiv 0 and m(0)=f(h)=h^2), with spike initial data h(x) = B\delta^{\bar\gamma}\phi(x/\delta); then \|\theta_0+h\|_{H^{\bar\gamma}} \lesssim B but \|m(0)\|_{L^2}/\|h\|_{L^2}^2 = \|h\|_{L^4}^2/\|h\|_{L^2}^2 \simeq \delta^{-d/2} \to \infty as \delta \to 0, and by time-continuity of w in H^{\bar\gamma} \subset L^\infty the \sup_t\|m(t)\|_{L^2} inherits this. Hence the quadratic estimate (quadap) is not proved by the displayed argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the \sup_t\|m(t)\|_{L^2} bound by an integrated one: the Duhamel/Gronwall form of the error equation gives \sup_t\|r(t)\|_{L^2} \lesssim \int_0^T \|m(s)\|_{L^2}ds \lesssim \|f''\|_\infty \int_0^T \|w(s)\|_{L^4}^2 ds; by Gagliardo-Nirenberg, \|w(s)\|_{L^4}^2 \lesssim \|w(s)\|_{H^1}^{d/2}\|w(s)\|_{L^2}^{2-d/2}, and the energy estimates \sup_t\|w(t)\|_{L^2} \lesssim \|h\|_{L^2} and \int_0^T\|w\|_{H^1}^2 \lesssim \|h\|_{L^2}^2 (both available in the paper) with Holder's inequality in time give \int_0^T\|w\|_{L^4}^2 \lesssim \|h\|_{L^2}^2 for d \le 3, restoring (quadap).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem linrob's conclusion - the quadratic linearisation bound (quadap), which verifies Condition C in Theorem bvminv and is used directly in the linearisation term I of Theorem ganzwien's proof - is unsupported as written.
issues.title: False L^2 bound on the Taylor remainder m in the proof of Theorem linrob
issues.why_classification: The conclusion and the quadratic rate survive, but because the displayed inequality itself is false, rescuing the result requires a genuinely different, contained argument (Duhamel representation plus Gagliardo-Nirenberg interpolation integrated in time) rather than a routine local correction; no substantive claim is lost once that argument is supplied.
